subject: pathology
title: Hepatitis, cirrhosis and liver failure

steps.tx: **Hepatitis** means hepatocyte injury with inflammation from viruses, alcohol, drugs, autoimmunity or ischaemia in different patients. It ranges from silent enzyme rises to fulminant failure, so necrosis pattern and cause guide prognosis more than symptoms alone. **Spotty lobular necrosis** marks acute viral injury, while **bridging necrosis** links vascular structures in severe attacks with worse outcome. **Interface hepatitis** at the limiting plate marks chronic active disease that continues to injure the liver over time.
steps.say: Hepatitis injures liver cells through viruses, alcohol, drugs, autoimmunity or poor blood supply in different patients. Bridging necrosis signals severe injury, while interface activity marks continuing chronic damage at the limiting plate. Cause and host immunity determine whether the liver recovers, scars or fails completely over time.

vis.alt: Histological image showing three patterns of liver necrosis: spotty lobular, bridging between vascular structures, and interface hepatitis at the limiting plate.
vis.caption: Hepatitis necrosis patterns: spotty, bridging, and interface

steps.tx: Viral serology decodes the stage of infection better than any single test, and examiners rotate these patterns repeatedly. **HBsAg** marks current hepatitis B infection, while anti HBs marks immunity from vaccination or past infection. **IgM anti HBc** marks acute or recent hepatitis B, and HBeAg marks high viral replication with greater infectivity. Hepatitis C antibody needs **RNA confirmation** for active infection, while hepatitis A and E spread by the faecal oral route.
steps.say: Surface antigen indicates current hepatitis B infection while surface antibody indicates immunity after vaccination or recovery. Core IgM marks acute disease, and hepatitis C needs RNA proof because antibody alone may reflect cleared infection. Hepatitis A and hepatitis E spread through the faecal oral route and usually cause acute disease.

With anti HBc means past natural infection

steps.tx: **Cirrhosis** is diffuse fibrosis with regenerative nodules that destroy normal liver architecture after any chronic liver injury. It remains irreversible once established, although treating its cause can prevent further decompensation and complications. **Portal hypertension** follows increased intrahepatic resistance with splanchnic vasodilation and produces ascites, varices and splenomegaly. Synthetic failure lowers albumin and clotting factors, while **encephalopathy** reflects gut derived toxins bypassing liver detoxification.
steps.say: Cirrhosis scars the whole liver into nodules and permanently distorts its normal architecture and blood flow. Portal pressure rises and causes ascites, varices and splenic enlargement over years of chronic injury. Failed synthesis and detoxification then cause clotting problems and encephalopathy that mark decompensated disease in patients.

left.title: Compensated cirrhosis
points: No ascites, variceal bleed, jaundice or encephalopathy yet
May be clinically silent with firm liver or splenomegaly
Surveillance for varices and liver cancer

right.title: Decompensated cirrhosis
points: Ascites, bleeding, jaundice or encephalopathy present
Infections and kidney failure precipitate decline

steps.tx: **Alcohol related hepatitis** adds steatosis, ballooned hepatocytes with **Mallory Denk bodies** and neutrophil rich inflammation inside injured liver tissue. Metabolic steatohepatitis mirrors the same pattern in obesity and diabetes without alcohol exposure in many patients. Mallory Denk bodies also appear in Wilson disease and drug injury, so they suggest alcohol rather than proving it alone. Abstinence and metabolic control remain the disease modifying treatments that slow further liver injury.
steps.say: Alcohol related hepatitis shows fat, ballooned cells, pink inclusions and neutrophils clustered around injured hepatocytes. Metabolic disease produces a similar pattern in obesity and diabetes without any alcohol exposure history. Those inclusions suggest alcohol strongly, but they also occur in other injuries and never prove cause alone.

steps.tx: The micrograph shows clear fat vacuoles of **steatosis** beside ballooned hepatocytes that contain pink **Mallory Denk bodies** marked as central hyaline. Neutrophils cluster around an injured hepatocyte in **neutrophil satellitosis**, which completes the classic alcoholic hepatitis picture at microscopy. This pattern matters because examiners use Mallory Denk bodies with steatosis and neutrophils to identify alcohol related hepatitis. Remember that similar bodies occur in metabolic and drug injury, so history remains essential.
steps.say: This micrograph shows fat vacuoles beside ballooned liver cells that contain pink hyaline inclusions inside their cytoplasm. Neutrophils cluster around one injured cell, and that satellitosis completes the alcoholic hepatitis pattern under microscopy. Examiners use this combination to identify alcohol related injury, although metabolic disease can look remarkably similar.

vis.caption: Steatosis with Mallory-Denk bodies and satellitosis. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Acute liver failure** combines coagulopathy with encephalopathy in a liver without prior cirrhosis and develops rapidly over days to weeks. Paracetamol overdose and viral hepatitis are classic causes whose importance varies by region and patient exposure. **Cerebral oedema** kills early, so head positioning, infection surveillance and urgent transplant referral cannot wait for deterioration. Chronic liver failure instead declares itself through decompensation events and hepatorenal physiology over a longer course.
steps.say: Acute liver failure means clotting failure plus encephalopathy developing rapidly without any prior cirrhosis history. Brain swelling kills early, so positioning, infection surveillance and transplant referral must happen without delay. Chronic failure develops differently because decompensation events accumulate gradually over months to years in most patients.
